critique.paragraph: This map teaches synthesis and retrospective organization, not authenticity collapse. It presents a clean museum of labeled methodologies — rhizome, commons, molecular design — with explicit categorization and no ambiguity. Edge M requires specimens of indeterminate provenance, forensic investigation, and the experience of not being able to tell (or of the question itself dissolving). Instead, this plate offers clarity, labels, and categorical organization. The visual grammar reads as 'gallery of approaches' not 'collapse of distinction.' The map may be an excellent capstone for its sequence, but it does not engage the real/synthetic edge at all.
strengths: Clear spatial organization with distinct stations creates navigable conceptual space
Miniature displays of prior maps provide effective retrospective framing
Surrounding darkness isolates and emphasizes the conceptual architecture
weaknesses: Zero engagement with provenance, authenticity, or real/synthetic distinction
Everything is explicitly labeled and categorized — opposite of Edge M's ambiguity requirement
No specimens to examine, no forensic tools, no investigative mechanics
No moment where the player cannot tell or where the question itself shifts
Reads as a foundations-crisis synthesis map, not an authenticity-collapse teaching
next_gen_hints: Replace all labeled stations with five unlabeled specimens (text fragments, visual works, code samples, recipes, sounds)
Provide forensic investigation tools: pattern analyzer, authorship detector, training-data tracer
Remove explicit labels entirely — make provenance the investigation, not the given
Design 2-3 specimens to be genuinely indeterminate: model-assisted human work, human-curated model output, mixed provenance
End with a reflection panel asking: 'Did wanting to know change how you read? Does the answer matter?'
Consider moving this map to Edge K (Incompleteness) or F (Transformation) where synthesis/retrospective fits better
If keeping for Edge M: introduce the Steyerl/Paglen framing — show works where the question of authenticity has already collapsed
